title: Concrete positive Tate-line product and permutation maps
statement:
Fix the finite purity coefficient setting [def-pur-conventions], A=O_E/(varpi_E^n), n≥1, and a separated finite-type k-scheme Y. Use the standard iterated affine-line realization of affine spaces [def-sbc-affine-space], the shifted finite Tate line L_Y=A_Y(1)[2] [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and its canonical pullback comparison [def-pur-affine-space-comparison]. Write Q_0(M)=M and Q_{r+1}(M)=Q_r(M)⊗M, so Q_r has r+1 factors. Put X_r=A_Y^{r+1}, p_r:X_r→Y, T_r=p_r^*Q_r(L_Y), and V_r=Rp_{r!}T_r using the finite constant-coefficient compact-support functor [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. At r=0 use the normalized affine-line compactification; otherwise use the published chosen compactification. Let t:V_0→A_Y be the normalized integration [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison], transported by the canonical Tate pullback and unit comparisons.
For a,b≥0, split the coordinates of X_{a+b+1} into the first a+1 and last b+1 coordinates. These give a Cartesian square over Y. Use the canonical pullback/tensor comparison and tensor associators to identify the external product T_a⊠T_b with T_{a+b+1}. It has bounded etale origin. Define λ_{a,b}:V_a⊗V_b→V_{a+b+1} to be precisely the chosen-compactification finite forward product [def-pur-finite-product-compactification-data], built from the actual finite exchange, projection and composition maps [def-exchange-projection], followed by that coefficient identification. If λ_{a,b} is invertible, define κ_{a,b} as its inverse. Given invertibility of λ_{r,0} for all r, define κ_0=id and κ_{r+1}=κ_{r,0} followed by κ_r⊗id. A nonempty planar binary tree has index number-of-leaves minus one, a parenthesized tensor of V_0, the canonical associator normalization to Q_r(V_0), and the forward iterate obtained by λ at every internal vertex. The tensor power t^{⊗(r+1)} uses the standard unit constraints. Define the signed tensor permutation using the canonical K-flat derived tensor symmetry [def-pur-finite-site-tensor-projection], associators and the last-factor decomposition of a finite permutation.
For σ a permutation of Fin(r+1), s_σ:X_r→X_r is the actual polynomial map pulling coordinate j back to coordinate σ(j). It is an isomorphism over Y and its square over id_Y is Cartesian. Identify s_σ^*T_r with T_r by the actual pullback compositor, since T_r is pulled from Y. Define S_σ on V_r by inverse identity pullback, compact-support exchange for this Cartesian square, the canonical compactification comparison [lem-pur-finite-forward-product-symmetry], and that coefficient identification. For each K in D^b_ctf(Y,A) [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], define S_{σ,K} in the same way on Rp_{r!}(p_r^*K⊗T_r), keeping K first and identifying its pullback by the compositor. The Tate objects and these coefficient-first objects, including their coordinate pullbacks, have bounded etale origin. The actual coefficient-first projection map [def-pur-finite-site-tensor-projection] K⊗V_r→Rp_{r!}(p_r^*K⊗T_r) is invertible. For J:V_r→A_Y define its coefficient-first integration as the inverse of that specific projection map followed by id_K⊗J and the right unitor. No six-functor datum, duality or purity is supplied.

proof.text: For block_geometry, prove by induction that morphisms to the iterated affine line are determined by their base map and all polynomial coordinates, using AffineSpace.hom_ext at the successor step. The two block maps commute with the base projection by toIteratedAffineLine_proj. Given maps to the two blocks with equal base maps, concatenate their coordinate vectors with Fin.addCases and apply toIteratedAffineLine. The coordinate equations prove both projection identities, and the same extensionality proves uniqueness. IsPullback.mk' gives the Cartesian square. This includes a=b=0 and arbitrary, possibly empty, bases.

For coordinate_geometry, compose the coordinate polynomial map for sigma with that for sigma inverse. Every coordinate and the base map are unchanged, so iterated-affine-line extensionality makes both composites identities. This exhibits the actual map as an isomorphism over Y. The square over id_Y is Cartesian by IsPullback.of_horiz_isIso.

The exponent ell^(level+1) is a unit on every scheme over k by exponentUnit. Apply finite_etale_torsion_twist_line to the finite scalar ring. Transport each localized trivialization across the over-site equivalence to obtain ordinary upperStar trivializations by the tensor unit. Its tensor inverse makes the sheaf finite; local constancy therefore makes it constructible. The flat degree-zero sheaf has Tor interval [0,0], and shift by 2 has interval [-2,-2]. Site comparison preserves bounded constructibility and Tor intervals. Hence shiftedLine is constructible of finite Tor amplitude.

Reflect a pro-etale finite-Tor bound to an ordinary bounded-constructible origin using the exact faithful monoidal site comparison. Apply the existing fixed-scalar ordinary constructibleFiniteTor_tensor and constructibleFiniteTor_mapDerivedCategory_upperStar theorems, and transport their conclusions by the canonical tensor and pullback comparison isomorphisms. Induction gives constructible finite-Tor positive tensor powers; pullback gives tate. Its bounded-etale-origin property transfers along externalIso, proving external_origin. The same tensor and pullback closure gives both clauses of coordinate_origins.

Apply the existing fixed-scalar hasProjectionFormulaOfCompactification_of_constructibleFiniteTor theorem to tate and K for the literal compactification. The coefficient-first projection is precisely the composite of the signed tensor symmetry, this canonical projection component, and compact-support image of the inverse-order symmetry. All three factors are isomorphisms, so their composite is an isomorphism. This is the published finite compact projection reduction before intrinsic-coefficient specialization.
